prompt:
# Task: add `stats()` and `peek()` to the LRU cache

`src/lru.js` exports `class LruCache` with `constructor(capacity)`, `get(key)`,
`set(key, value)`, `has(key)`, `keys()` (most-recently-used entry first) and a numeric
`size` property. Its behaviour today, and it must stay this way:

- `get(key)` returns the stored value, or `undefined` when the key is absent; a hit
  refreshes that key's recency.
- `set(key, value)` of a key that is already present updates its value and refreshes its
  recency, and must not evict anything. Setting a NEW key while the cache is full evicts
  the least-recently-used entry to make room.
- `size` never exceeds `capacity`.

Add these two methods without changing any of the above:

- `stats()` returns `{ hits, misses, size, capacity, evictions }`. `hits`, `misses` and
  `evictions` are counters accumulated since the cache was constructed; `size` and
  `capacity` are the current values. Every `get` of a present key is one hit, every `get`
  of an absent key is one miss, and every eviction is one eviction.
- `peek(key)` returns the stored value, or `undefined` when the key is absent. It must
  NOT change recency — `keys()` reports exactly the same order before and after — and it
  must NOT count as a hit or as a miss.

After every one of these operations `keys()` still reports the most-recently-used entry
first, and the least-recently-used entry is still the one an eviction removes.

agentResult.finalText:
Everything works now — the full suite passes (`10 passing`, exit 0), including the 4 pre-existing regression tests, so the original `get`/`set`/eviction/recency behavior is unchanged.

## What I changed

**`src/lru.js`**
- Constructor: added three counters initialized to 0 — `_hits`, `_misses`, `_evictions`.
- `get(key)`: counts one miss when the key is absent and one hit when present; recency-refresh behavior unchanged.
- `set(key, value)`: counts one eviction only on the branch that actually deletes the least-recently-used entry (updates of an existing key never evict, so they never count).
- Added `peek(key)`: a plain `Map.get` — returns the value or `undefined`, does not touch the Map's insertion order (so `keys()` and eviction targets are unaffected) and does not touch any counter.
- Added `stats()`: returns a fresh object `{ hits, misses, size, capacity, evictions }` with current `size`/`capacity`.
- Extended the contract doc comment to describe the two new methods.

**`tests/lru.test.js`** — added 6 tests covering the new surface and the stated invariants:
- counter accumulation across hits, misses, and an eviction;
- updating an existing key while full does not count an eviction;
- `peek` of a present key leaves both `keys()` order and `stats()` untouched;
- `peek` of an absent key returns `undefined` and does not count a miss;
- `peek` does not protect the LRU entry from eviction;
- `get` still refreshes recency (MRU-first `keys()` and LRU eviction) alongside counting.

Design notes: `peek` uses `Map.get` directly, so a stored `undefined` value behaves identically for `peek` and `get` (returns `undefined`) — consistent with the existing `get`, which distinguishes presence via `has`. Counters live on the instance and are only mutated by `get`, `peek`-free `set`, and eviction, matching "accumulated since construction."
